transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining me. As you know, we're looking at a proposed eighth-grade makerspace program for the spring semester, and before I make a final authorization decision, I'd like to gather input from each of you based on your areas of expertise. The draft proposes 24 students supervised by one STEM teacher, meeting twice weekly, using soldering stations, hand tools, a laser cutter, standard metal components, and cloud-based CAD files. I'd like to go around and hear any concerns or recommendations you each have regarding implementation. Who would like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to flag an important safety issue. I completed a room-safety review this week, and it found that the makerspace may enroll no more than 16 students. Additionally, any session using soldering stations with more than 12 students requires two supervising adults. The draft program form still shows the original numbers of 24 students with one STEM teacher, so those will need to be revised before the program can be safely authorized.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to raise a health concern. My review of the participating students' health records found one student with a documented severe nickel allergy. That student may participate only when the program uses nickel-free components, and I must approve the materials list before each session. I should also note that this health-record review has not yet been added to the program file, so we need to make sure it's documented before authorization.
